articles.title: Former global sensation Fiona the hippo dies after eating a visitor's hat
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Zoo announced Thursday that its famed hippo Fiona has died 11 days after swallowing a knit cap that slipped into her enclosure. She was nine years old. "It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency," the zoo said in a statement. The zoo's animal care team spent days trying to help Fiona pass the obstruction, going so far as to use a vibration plate borrowed from a horse farm to help shake it through her digestive tract. An ultrasound showed bunching in Fiona's intestines; a colonoscopy with a 9-foot scope didn't help, nor did a "giant" enema. It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency. https://t.co/X0GVbDAiEQ pic.twitter.com/7wLF0uclWB — Cincinnati Zoo (@CincinnatiZoo) November 19, 2026 Specialists said surgery wasn't an option for a full-grown Nile hippopotamus. "They have a multichambered stomach for digesting plants — sort of like a cow — but they don't regurgitate and chew cud like a cow does," Jack Kottwitz, an assistant professor at Michigan State University's College of Veterinary Medicine, told the Associated Press . "Those multiple chambers, tissue folds, fluid, and digesting food easily 'hide' the hat, making removal with an endoscope from the stomach chambers very difficult." Hippos are also difficult to anesthetize and then keep away from water as they heal. Zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley told the AP that Fiona ingested the knit hat on Nov. 8 after it was tossed in the air by a visitor and flung by a ceiling fan through a small opening above the viewing windows of her enclosure. Fiona was no stranger to health struggles; she became a sensation after she was born six weeks premature in 2017. At the time, she couldn't stand on her own and weighed just 29 pounds; the next smallest Nile hippo on record weighed roughly twice as much at birth. Zoo staff had to bottle-feed Fiona with a mixture of formula and her mother's milk. (A hippopotamus had never been hand-milked before.) While teething, Fiona began to refuse the bottle, and clinicians from Cincinnati Children's Hospital were called in to administer fluids intravenously. Fiona in 2020. John Minchillo/AP But soon Fiona began to thrive. Named after Shrek's love interest, Princess Fiona — zoo staff said her ears had a similar shape — she went on to star in her own show on YouTube and other platforms. Her plight — and her adorable triumph over adversity — inspired a host of children's books, a line of beer, a bobblehead and even a limited-edition ice cream flavor. Fiona also became a Cincinnati icon. Her character in the Cincinnati Ballet's 2018 production of Nutcracker reportedly " stole the show "; the same year, a Fiona mural was unveiled downtown. "Our city is heartbroken," Mayor Aftab Pureval wrote on social media, "but we couldn't be more grateful that she was part of our lives and our community as a whole." Amy Acton, Ohio’s incoming governor, posted that Fiona’s survival story “brought joy, hope and a little extra magic to our state.” This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/article/fiona-the-hippo-dies-after-swallowing-hat-in-freak-accident-at-the-cincinnati-zoo-211146772.html

articles.title: Senate Republicans quash resolution curbing Trump's Iran war powers
articles.summary: By Patricia Zengerle WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - US Senate Republicans on Thursday rejected legislation directing President Donald Trump to end the war in Iran or obtain Congress' approval to continue, backing the president weeks ‌after sweeping defeats in midterm elections largely tied to Americans' frustration with the conflict. The Senate voted 51 ‌to 48, largely along party lines, to defeat a war powers resolution that had previously passed the House of Representatives. The US Constitution says that ​only Congress, not the president, can declare war, and Democrats have argued that Trump may have pulled the country into a long conflict by failing to spell out a clear strategy. Only three Republicans - Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and Rand Paul of Kentucky - voted with Democrats in favor of the resolution. One Democrat, John Fetterman of Pennsylvania, voted with ‌Republicans against it. The vote was the first ⁠on the conflict since Democratic victories in the midterm elections on November 3. Trump's fellow Republicans, who rarely break with the president, stood behind him in support of the US-Israeli war ⁠on Iran that started on February 28. Just 31% of Americans approve of the US war on Iran, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted November 13-16. It was the 21st vote in Congress on a war powers resolution since the war began. Democrats said ​they filed ​the measure to put Republicans on the record as supporting ​the war. SHOWDOWN LOOMS IN 2027 Democrats will control large ‌majorities in the House and Senate next year, and party leaders have pledged to make ending the war a top priority once they take over on January 3, setting the stage for a potential showdown with Trump. Democratic Senator Tim Kaine of Virginia, who has called repeatedly for Congress to take back its control over declarations of war, said the midterm election result reflected Americans' unhappiness about the war, and higher prices for food, fuel and other goods linked to ‌the conflict. "Its unpopularity was made absolutely, manifestly clear in the election ​results of November 3," Kaine said in a speech before the vote ​appealing for yes votes. Democrats made affordability a theme ​of the election campaign. Democrats have also balked at the cost of the foreign conflict, at a ‌time when Republicans have been cutting domestic programs ​like health insurance subsidies and ​free school lunches. Pentagon data in late October showed that the US military had spent over $47 billion to prosecute the war, more than 25% higher than the Defense Department's estimate in July. The latest resolution had passed the ​House in mid-September by 220-204, reflecting lawmakers' ‌growing unhappiness with the months-long conflict weeks before the midterms. A similar measure passed both the Senate and ​House earlier this year, but the Trump administration ignored it, saying it was not legally binding. (Reporting ​by Patricia Zengerle; Editing by Don Durfee and Alistair Bell) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/us-senate-rejects-resolution-curbing-195349892.html

articles.title: JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard disclose cyberattack on third-party vendors
articles.summary: JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ), Visa ( V ), and Mastercard ( MA ) said on Thursday that some select customer data, including names and emails, was accessed by attackers after a cyberattack on a vendor. Spokespeople for the companies said no payments or card data was leaked and that their own systems were not affected by the incident. JPMorgan said it believes hackers who attacked a third-party vendor accessed marketing data, including customer names and email addresses. The bank also said the incident isn't related to outages many of its customers reported earlier this week, which it blamed on a software bug . "Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses," a JPMorgan spokesperson said. "We were recently informed of an incident at a third-party provider that resulted in the exposure of limited amount of email addresses – non-payments information – from a small subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program," a Mastercard spokesperson said. "There is no impact to the Mastercard payment network or the ability for people to use their cards," the person added. A Visa spokesperson added claims of the incident are associated to a third-party service provider in the Asia Pacific region. "This is unrelated to any of the system disruptions across different industries this past week," the Visa spokesperson added. A ransomware group known as n0n has claimed responsibility for the attacks on the dark web and shared sample data as proof, according to cybersecurity firm SOCRadar. The cybersecurity firm told Yahoo Finance that it hasn't independently verified whether the ransomware group carried out the intrusion. It also supported JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard's statements that the breaches most likely originated at a third-party vendor and involved marketing and benefit-program data such as names and email addresses. "The most immediate risk for consumers is targeted phishing that impersonates their bank or card provider," SOCRadar chief information security officer Ensar Seker said in an emailed statement. The latest incident comes as consumers are on high alert after a string of major technology outages this November . The Wall Street Journal earlier reported the connection between the breaches and the ransomware group. Follow David Hollerith on X @DsHollers . articles.title: Some Americans say they're 'prepping for survival' after recent major tech outages
articles.summary: Canning fruits was a hobby for Korrie Roth until Microsoft Outlook went down. And then the planes stopped flying. And then Apple Pay froze up. And then the National Security Agency, whose responsibilities include defending the government from cyberattacks, reported its own mysterious outage. “Now I’m prepping for survival,” said Roth, a 37-year-old IT specialist and mother of five, who lives in Greenwood, Indiana. Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post. No explanation from the country’s leaders has soothed her. President Donald Trump suggesting everything is “fine” on Tuesday lacked empathy, she thought. She was not feeling fine, and her social media feeds were full of panicked friends asking some version of: What is going on? “You’re supposed to trust the government to give you information and protect you,” she said. “But we are worried, and the government is just like, ‘Oh, you’re silly.’” Roth bought a crank radio and extra bottled water and checked in with someone she actually trusts right now - her father. He bought a portable generator during the Microsoft crash, he told her. A slew of seemingly unrelated outages, coupled with media reports both vague and menacing, have led to a groundswell of worry from Americans who said they’re preparing for a bevy of worst-case scenarios: Widespread power outages? Electrical grid failure? The end of the world? The political response has offered little clarity. Some Republicans have amplified suspicions that the outages are connected. “The American people can see everything happening with these service outages, and they feel like they’re not getting the whole story,” Sen. Rick Scott (R-Florida) wrote Tuesday on X, demanding transparency from companies and federal agencies. Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Missouri) was more pointed. “If this is all a coincidence, it’s like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world,” he told reporters at the Capitol. The administration, by contrast, has sought to tamp down speculation. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Tuesday he understood why people are nervous but the government had “zero evidence” linking the outages. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told the House Homeland Security Committee in a Wednesday hearing that while Americans are right to ask questions, “these are separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes. They are not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack.” But on the internet, where “preppers” are sharing tips on Facebook groups and Reddit communities, nothing seems outside the realm of possibility - especially to people who have long maintained that they’re prepared for anything. One 60-year-old retired aircraft mechanic restocked his pantry, adding a solar-based power station to charge electronics, 16 small propane tanks, a large propane tank and a portable heater. In the past month, he estimates he has spent about $3,500 on additional supplies. Though Camille Sibert, a 25-year-old stay-at-home mom in Indiana, said she has been a prepper for three years, the week’s chaos has vindicated her decision to think ahead. Amid news of the outages, she and her husband went to Walmart and bought canned goods, gallon jugs of water, vitamins and over-the-counter medication. They also filled up their vehicles with gas. “I try to avoid panic buying, but with everything going on in current events we’d rather be safe than sorry,” she said. She used to think of prepping as a hypothetical, but it feels more real now. “It started as a scenario ... to think about and consider how I would respond and survive,” she said. “But now, so many odd things have happened recently that the thought of a power grid shutdown doesn’t seem so ‘crazy’ anymore.” Whitney Phillips, a University of Oregon professor who studies information politics, said that when people receive a barrage of alarming fragments from fractured sources, they often feel compelled to fill in the gaps to make sense of the news. “There’s too much to sort through,” she said, “and then we’re making a kind of mental shortcut to try to just get through our days and make sense of things.” Increased uncertainty, according to Phillips, can push people already inclined toward apocalyptic thinking further in that direction. “It doesn’t take very much to push them over that edge.” But the proclivity to stock up isn’t isolated to those who consider themselves preppers. David Bellinger, a senior analyst at the investment bank Mizuho Securities, noted in a Monday research report that shoppers have been swarming Costco in recent days with “emergency prep sales.” As of Sunday night, he noted, 21 of the 26 most expensive generators were sold out on the company’s website. Costco did not respond to a request for comment. Two officials at the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media, said they were concerned themselves about the string of outages and were having trouble believing they were a coincidence. One official described the barrage of messages they received from former high school classmates asking whether they should be prepping for a massive emergency; another said they took out extra cash. “There is nothing on this scale that has happened before in this many sectors this close together,” one of the officials said. “This is scary, and there is no leadership.” FEMA did not respond to a request for comment. At a time of heightened uncertainty, leaders - of a company or a country - can ease anxiety with clear, detailed information, said John Rogula, a veteran risk manager who is a principal at the global consultancy Baker Tilly’s risk advisory practice. “You’re going to have a lot less panic if you have a plan,” he said. Those in charge set the tone, he added. Shrugging off concerns can amplify them. “You need to be transparent in regards to your readiness,” Rogula said. The Trump administration’s attempts to downplay concerns contrasted with the response in Europe, which has experienced cyberattacks on supermarket fridges and hoax bomb threats in recent weeks. In Britain, government officials launched a “Be Ready” campaign in October, encouraging people to stock up on enough bottled water and food to last three days. Last year, the European ​Commission announced a preparedness strategy that also aims to have citizens self-sufficient for a minimum of 72 hours, with supplies of food, water, power generators and medicines. While some Americans are rushing to prepare for a world without power, others have spent years laying the groundwork. Shawn Hendrix, 49, a burly survivalist and former operations chief for the popular YouTuber MrBeast, describes himself as a self-sufficient homesteader who lives off the electric grid on a solar-powered farm full of animals. From his farm in eastern North Carolina where he was “out moving cows,” he said the recent outages have not fazed him, because he has been planning for decades. “If it happens, it won’t be one of these, ’oh no on this date X is going to happen,’ it will just happen,” he said. “Don’t be scared be prepared. Then just live your life.” Despite her own fears, Roth, the IT specialist who has been canning fruits and buying supplies, flew this week to Washington, D.C., for work. The planes were flying again, the ground stop lifted, but delays were still rampant, and she kept checking her phone for updates. “In the back of your mind, you’re like, well it’s probably going to be just fine,” Roth said. Then she paused. “But, what if it’s not? articles.title: Thanksgiving travel could get stormier on the way home as El Niño strengthens
articles.summary: With Thanksgiving a week away and El Niño still strengthening , holiday travelers face increased odds of stormy weather in parts of the South, while the Caribbean may stay drier. The climate pattern, which occurs when waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean become unusually warm, can shift weather patterns across the country, potentially affecting popular winter getaways from Florida to the Caribbean. NOAA's Climate Prediction Center said on Nov. 12 that El Niño is still strengthening, with a greater-than-79 % chance of a strong-to-very-strong event between January and March 2027. That's down from 83% in its October update, but it’s still likely to produce adverse conditions, with wetter weather in the South and warmer weather in the North. "El Niños are associated with more storminess across the southern tier of the country, and potentially more ice storms across the southern plains," Matthew Rosencrans, a meteorologist at NOAA's Weather Prediction Center, told Yahoo Travel in October. Those conditions can significantly disrupt travel, the meteorologist said, but the effects will be far from uniform. El Niño winters are also often warmer, Rosencrans explains, which can sometimes benefit travel across the northern tier of the contiguous U.S. Meanwhile, parts of the Caribbean may see drier weather, creating very different conditions for travelers depending on their destination. What it means for Thanksgiving week NOAA's Climate Prediction Center outlook , released on Thursday, Nov. 19, said the strong El Niño will be the major influence on U.S. weather this winter, with wetter-than-normal conditions favored across the southern tier of the country and the Southeast. The outlook covers December through February rather than Thanksgiving week itself, but it points to a stormier backdrop for winter travel in the South. Though slightly fewer people are expected to travel by car or plane for Thanksgiving this year, the AAA still expects 81.5 million people to travel at least 50 miles over the holiday. Bus, train and cruise travel is projected to increase. No single storm is expected to disrupt travel nationwide before Thanksgiving, AccuWeather reports, but the most persistent wet weather will be in the Southeast, following heavy rain and flooding in Florida this week. Periods of rain and thunderstorms from the Gulf Coast into the Southeast early in the week could cause delays at major connecting hubs such as Atlanta and Charlotte, affecting travelers flying on to Florida and the Caribbean. Return trips could be rougher, with conditions potentially becoming much stormier across much of the East right after the holiday. Where winter travelers could feel the effects Travelers heading to Florida this winter for a holiday getaway could face wetter-than-usual conditions, with El Niño increasing the likelihood of rainfall and severe weather across parts of the Southeast. "For Florida, it often means a fairly robust secondary severe weather season in November and into December across the Southeast and Florida," Rosencrans says. NOAA's outlook gives Florida, southern Georgia and the coastal Carolinas the greatest likelihood of a wetter-than-normal winter, with a greater than 70% chance of above-normal precipitation for December through February. Temperatures are expected to be near normal across parts of the Southeast, though forecasters note considerable uncertainty and say a shift in Atlantic air-pressure patterns, known as a negative North Atlantic Oscillation, could bring cooler spells. That doesn't necessarily mean travelers need to rethink a Florida vacation, but those hoping for uninterrupted beach weather should keep an eye on the forecast. The winter seasonal precipitation outlook, according to NOAA. NOAA While Florida could see a wetter winter, the Caribbean islands may see less rain, though it varies by island and time of year. Rosencrans said the Caribbean can often see drier weather during El Niño events, though the effect is strongest in summer. The ABC islands (Aruba, Bonaire and Curaçao) are one example of where less rain is likely. Their main rainy season typically runs from October through January, with the dry season arriving later, from February through May. An El Niño suppresses that rainy season, according to the Meteorological Department of Curaçao . While lower rainfall over the islands may sound appealing, Rosencrans says it can mean fewer thunderstorms and make days feel hotter "as there is less cloudiness and continuous sunshine." How did El Niño affect hurricane season? While El Niño suppressed Atlantic activity this year, the National Hurricane Center is now watching a possible late-season system off the Southeast coast this weekend, giving it a 60% chance of becoming a subtropical or tropical storm within seven days. Lindsey Long, a meteorologist at NOAA's Weather Prediction Center, told Yahoo in October that, "in a typical year, we would expect about two additional hurricanes to develop between mid-October and Nov. 30." The upcoming storm, which would be named Kyle, will affect the weather even if it doesn't develop further. Forecasters expect strong winds, dangerous surf and coastal flooding along parts of the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic coasts into the early part of Thanksgiving week. What travelers should watch for next Beyond this weekend's possible storm, the bigger risks for winter travelers are likely to be storms and delays rather than tropical systems. NOAA's Climate Prediction Center expects El Niño to remain strong through the winter, peaking around the turn of the year, and to persist through spring before a shift to neutral conditions becomes more likely between April and June. The agency's next El Niño update is due on Dec. 10, with its next seasonal outlook following on Dec. 17. Travelers heading to the South or the Caribbean may want to consider flexible booking options and check their travel insurance to see which weather-related disruptions are covered, including delays and cancellations caused by winter storms. articles.title: Key takeaways from the historic summit between Trump, Xi and Putin
articles.summary: SHENZHEN, China (AP) — The meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump, China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin on Thursday was the first-ever sit-down for the leaders of the three countries. They started with talk of a shared responsibility for keeping peace as the victors of World War II and as global powers. But post-meeting readouts by the three nations reflected more symbolism than substance. The “peace declaration” released after their meeting made no mention of Russia's war in Ukraine or the U.S.-led war in Iran. It said they agreed on the need for reforms to the United Nations, on increasing oil supplies and on reducing nuclear risks. The statement did not spell out the type and extent of the U.N. reforms the leaders agreed to. The three sides also agreed that state officials should enjoy immunity from prosecution, opposing what they called “jurisdiction abuse” by the International Criminal Court, the reports said. Here are key takeaways from the talks, which lasted over an hour. China's Xi presided over the summit of 21st century powers Xi added to China’s already burgeoning diplomatic stature merely by hosting the event. He said the talks with Trump and Putin were positive and fruitful, and that the three nations had aligned views on safeguarding world peace, according to China's Xinhua official news agency. They agreed major powers should take the legitimate security concerns of all countries seriously and believe differences should be resolved through negotiation and cooperation, Xinhua reported. “As long as dialogue does not stop, doors remain open, there is hope for peace,” Xi was quoted as saying. “The seeds planted at today’s trilateral meeting will surely take root, sprout, blossom and bear fruit.” China's insistence that it has the right to recover the democratically governed island of Taiwan, possibly by force, was not addressed in the leaders' broadly worded agreement. China considers that a domestic issue. China likes to position itself as a different kind of superpower from the U.S. and Russia — one that doesn’t get involved in wars and advocates for smaller states, said Ruby Osman, a senior policy adviser at London’s Tony Blair Institute for Global Change. Beijing’s priority was steering the meeting away from specifics, she said. “Beijing wanted to be seen as the adult in the room.” Trump claims a place in history Trump heralded the leaders’ gathering as “really making history” and he suggested to Xi and Putin that together they were shaking things up by ditching the “old school” way adversaries engage. The White House set low expectations for the talks. But Trump framed them Thursday as only the beginning — a chance to get the conversation rolling on solving some of the world's thorniest issues. “A lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start,” Trump told Putin during a one-on-one meeting prior to their three-way meeting with Xi. The carefully crafted event was a welcome break for Trump after a couple of rotten weeks for his presidency in which his Republican Party was trounced in the midterm elections, widespread tech outages spooked Americans, and Iran escalated attacks on U.S. allies. Trump said Iran was on the agenda as was Russia's war against Ukraine. China and Russia carry enormous sway with Tehran and also have been accused by the U.S. of supporting the Islamic Republic. He reiterated Thursday that he and Xi agree Iran needs to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for world energy supplies that has become a chokepoint since the start of the war. They also agree that Iran cannot obtain a nuclear weapon, Trump said. But there were no signs that Trump secured any agreements from Xi or Putin to help solve the Iran conflict. Following the talks, Trump dialed into a meeting in Berlin between U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alongside more than 40 European leaders who are supporting Ukraine’s war effort. Trump told the Berlin gathering that he spoke to Xi and Putin about finding a peaceful end to the Ukraine war, Witkoff said. Putin shares spotlight with Trump and Xi For Putin, the three-way talks on the sidelines of the APEC summit — and his meetings with both leaders separately earlier — offered a much-coveted chance for the Kremlin leader to signal that he heads a superpower on par with the United States and China. Trump and Putin found common ground in their opposition to the ICC. The Russian leader is wanted by the ICC under an arrest warrant for his alleged war crimes in Ukraine. The U.S. opposes the ICC’s arrest warrant against former Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Putin last attended an APEC summit in 2017. His presence as an honored guest and Russia's status as a top global power — at least at the gathering in Shenzhen — mark a diplomatic breakthrough. Just before the summit, Russia sent a pair of nuclear-capable Tu-95 bombers on a visit to Vietnam in a reminder of its nuclear might. And as Putin arrived in China, Russian TV zeroed in on an officer in his retinue who was carrying a briefcase with the codes for Moscow’s nuclear forces. Putin addressed Xi as “dear friend” during their talks on Wednesday, and smiled contentedly on Thursday as he shook hands with Trump, who called him “my friend” and boasted about their “great relationship for many years.” Speaking at the start of the three-way talks, Putin underscored the global weight of Russia, China and the U.S. The three nations are “united not only by our status as victors in World War II, but, most importantly, by our shared responsibility for maintaining international peace and security,” he said. They are also among the founders of the United Nations, Putin noted, adding that “we bear responsibility for preserving and strengthening the system of international law.” “Our nations share many common interests regarding the resolution of regional conflicts, including, of course, the conflict in Ukraine,” Putin said. Russia’s war in Ukraine featured in Putin’s bilateral meetings with Trump and Xi. It wasn’t the main topic of the three-way talks, Putin’s spokesman Dmitry Peskov said. The Kremlin released video of the Chinese leader escorting the Russian president to his car at the end of the talks and the two men shaking hands. “I don’t think anyone even expected things to go so well,” Putin told Xi as the two men parted ways. ___ Madhani reported from Washington and Leung reported from Hong Kong. articles.title: Little League player dies 6 months after being hit by baseball
articles.summary: Xavier Taylor, a 12-year-old Little League baseball player from New Jersey who was injured after being hit by a baseball in May, has died, his family announced. Taylor was critically injured while warming up before a May 26 game when he was accidentally hit by a baseball in the neck. He was airlifted from Maple Shade, New Jersey, to Cooper University Hospital in Camden. The teenager was placed in a coma after suffering cardiac arrest. "For the past five and a half months, the Nation has been lit up by the life of a remarkable 12-year-old boy from Maple Shade, New Jersey, Xavier Taylor," read a statement from the the Xavier Strong All Things Foundation said on social media "Xavier beat the odds of what doctors said would be impossible." View this post on Instagram In a show of support as Taylor was hospitalized, the Philadelphia skyline and city landmarks, including the Ben Franklin Bridge, were lit up in blue during a June night . Local communities also showed their solidarity with the Little Leaguer by wearing his No. 6 jersey and placing baseball bats outside their homes. A meal train raised over $141,000 for the family. The baseball world joined in with support as well. Philadelphia Phillies catcher Garrett Stubbs visited Taylor in June and gave him a signed bat; the Trenton Thunder of the MLB Draft League honored him before a game; and the Tampa Bay Rays sent the family a video . Taylor would have turned 13 on Nov. 27. "Thank you for being the light that you were on this earth. We will miss you, but your legacy will live on. We love you Xave," the foundation said. articles.title: Voyager 1 phones home from a light-day away for the 1st time in space history
articles.summary: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — NASA’s Voyager 1 has phoned home from one light-day away , humanity’s first emissary to cross this monumental threshold way out in interstellar space . Flight controllers received the spacecraft’s call Thursday, exactly 24 hours after it was sent. That’s how long it took for the radio signal to traverse the more than 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers) at the speed of light. “Voyager 1 light-day distance confirmed ... Voyager 1 continues its journey into the unknown,” controller Nshan Kazaryan announced to cheers and applause. For a spacecraft already loaded with historic firsts, it was an especially momentous milestone. “Once again Voyager breaking records, breaking boundaries and taking humanity on a voyage,” NASA’s science mission chief Nicky Fox said. “There’s no end for the Voyager mission.” Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 swept past Jupiter in 1979 and Saturn in 1980, snapped the most distant photo ever taken of our “Pale Blue Dot” in 1990, became the most distant human-made object in 1998, and crossed from the sun’s sphere of influence into the vast void between stars in 2012. NASA could not confirm the newest distance record until the signal reached the control team at California's Jet Propulsion Laboratory via the deep space telescope near Madrid. But that didn’t stop the space agency from wishing everyone a “Happy Voyager light-day … day!” via social media on Wednesday. Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, are NASA’s longest-operating space missions, churning out data for nearly a half-century despite powering down most of their instruments to keep exploring. Voyager 2 actually beat its twin into space by two weeks. But its route to Jupiter and Saturn plus Uranus and Neptune was slower and longer, and it did not reach interstellar space until 2018. It won’t reach the one-light-day mark until 2035. Both spacecraft are doing well for their 49 years of age, plowing through space at 38,000 mph (61,000 kph) with plutonium for power. Picture-taking ended long ago, but they typically send back bits of precious data almost every day on their never-before-explored environment. Over the weekend, though, Voyager 1's stream of science and engineering data came to an abrupt halt. The carrier signal that normally conveys that data kept coming in strong and, along with flight path calculations, allowed the team to confirm the light-day milestone. Controllers are trying to figure out why the flow of science and engineering data stopped. A similar problem three years ago was traced to an onboard computer. Each Voyager carries a so-called Golden Record brimming with the sounds of Earth. The project was led by the late Cornell University astronomer Carl Sagan, who also coined the phrase “Pale Blue Dot” for Voyager 1’s farewell glimpse of Earth. NASA expects the gold-plated phonographic records — time capsules for anyone or anything that might encounter them — to last more than 1 billion years. “No matter how long it takes or how dark things get or what we think our limitations are, we should never stop shining and never stop reaching for the stars. For we never know how far we will go,” said deputy project scientist Jamie Rankin of Princeton University. “Shine on, Voyager, shine on.” ___ The Associated Press’ health and science coverage receives financial support from the AP Fund for Journalism and private foundations. articles.title: SpaceX周四拟发债60亿美元，完成全部320亿美元债券融资，用于购买英伟达芯片
articles.summary: SpaceX正寻求在周四完成至少320亿美元的债务发售，为英伟达AI芯片采购提供资金。 据彭博援引知情人士透露， 本次发售包括约60亿美元债券，规模已从此前的40亿美元上调，于周四向投资者开放认购；其余约260亿美元票据此前已完成配售。 全部320亿美元债务定于周四定价，债务由三部分组成。高盛与Apollo主导此次交易。 这笔融资的特殊之处在于结构。 资金将通过名为Saturn Funding Trust的特殊目的载体购买英伟达AI芯片，该载体由Apollo支持的一家实体管理，SpaceX初期以约五年期租约使用这些芯片。 债务偿付与租金挂钩，而融资安排使借款不进入SpaceX资产负债表，公司预计借此维持投资级信用评级。在AI竞赛中，高评级往往被视为关键竞争优势，它意味着能更快、更多地借钱。 SpaceX在10月表示，贝莱德、高盛资产管理以及KKR集团旗下的账户均是最新这笔交易的基石投资者。本次发行依据美国证券交易委员会（SEC）的相关规定进行，可向符合条件的境内外机构广泛营销，但不得面向部分零售投资者。 截至发稿，SpaceX股价周四盘中下跌4.5%，英伟达股价下跌2.3%。 三层结构，一笔出表融资 这笔债务被拆分为三部分，具体条款未对外披露。 60亿美元债券面向投资者公开发售，规模较早前计划增加20亿美元，显示认购需求强劲；剩余约260亿美元票据在此前已直接配售给资金管理机构。 对这一结构而言，真正的关键在于会计处理：芯片由特殊目的载体持有，SpaceX以承租人身份出现，债务不计入公司资产负债表。 对一家正在大举投入AI基础设施的公司来说，这一点至关重要。科技行业正把数以万亿美元计的资金投向数据中心与AI基础设施，并大量举债支持。评级一旦被下调，融资成本和融资速度都会立刻受到影响。 维持高评级，是竞争优势 SpaceX首席财务官Bret Johnsen在上月发布业绩后的投资者电话会上，强调了公司“强劲的投资级资产负债表”。 这一表述出现在公司完成大规模股权与债券融资之后：SpaceX在6月的首次公开募股中售出862亿美元股票，数日后又定价发行250亿美元高评级公司债券。 本次芯片融资延续了同一思路——在不推高资产负债表杠杆的前提下，继续扩大算力投入。将债务置于表外，使公司能够在不牺牲评级的情况下加杠杆，这对处在资本开支竞赛中的大型科技企业尤为重要。 分销更广，买家更多 SEC规则下的发行方式，让这笔债券可以触达更广的机构群体。 Manulife Investment Management固收高级投资组合经理Jeff Given表示，这带来了广泛分销与灵活性，意味着债券可能“落入更多投资者手中”。对于一笔规模超过300亿美元的发行而言，投资者基础的宽度直接关系到定价与二级市场表现。 从6月的IPO、随后的高评级债券，到如今的芯片租赁融资，SpaceX在数月内搭建起一套多层次的资本结构。周四的定价结果，将检验市场对AI相关债务的胃口还能承接多大的供给。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 苹果赢下英国用户数据诉讼首回合，政府秘密令状被迫公开
articles.summary: 苹果在与英国政府的隐私拉锯战中赢下了关键一局。 11月19日，据彭博报道， 英国调查权力法庭作出最新裁决，认定英国内政部“未能证明”公开秘密命令会损害国家安全 。这意味着，与以往绝大多数全程保密的监控案件不同， 苹果及两家非营利组织发起的这场法律挑战，接下来大部分程序将首次在公开法庭上进行。 此前，英国政府依据法律秘密向苹果发出一份“技术能力通知”（TCN），要求苹果交出用户的加密数据。 按照英国法律，这类命令附带严格的“封口令”，收到通知的公司甚至不能对外承认命令的存在，政府也一直以“国家安全”为由拒绝公开。苹果随后向专门审查秘密监控的英国调查权力法庭提起诉讼。 苹果发言人对此表示欢迎，称这是朝着信息透明迈出的正确一步。英国内政部则试图淡化影响，强调这只是一次“程序性裁定”，尚未决定苹果最终是否必须交出数据，并强硬表态称“关系英国公众安全的决定应由政府和法官作出，而不是科技公司的董事会”。 尽管这场关于“苹果该不该削弱加密”的核心较量才刚刚开始，但此次裁决打破了政府的保密护盾，把原本只能靠媒体猜测的暗箱博弈推到了阳光下。对市场和投资者而言，未来围绕苹果英国产品功能受限、合规成本上升的评估，也将拥有更透明的依据。 法庭：公开令状不会损害国家安全 据彭博报道，调查权力法庭（Investigatory Powers Tribunal）是一个独立司法机构，专门审视英国情报与监控部门的秘密行动。 在周四公开的裁决中，该法庭指出，关于TCN存在的消息已多次泄露给媒体，其中包括《金融时报》，而英国政府还曾在华盛顿与美国官员讨论此事。法庭认为，这些做法构成对"既不确认也不否认"（NCND）政策的"重大偏离"。 法庭的措辞相当直接：这些偏离的"累积效应"是，任何对该议题略有兴趣的人都已经知道英国内政部向苹果发出了技术能力通知。 因此，官方确认该令状会损害国家安全、或向"恶意行为者"提供新信息，这一说法是"荒诞的"（fanciful）。 内政部打破沉默，首次承认令状存在 自2025年2月有关TCN的消息首次曝光以来，英国政府一直拒绝就苹果案置评。周四，这一沉默被打破。 英国内政部确认了技术能力通知的存在，并称该通知"仅仅"要求苹果"维持相应能力"，以按法律要求协助警方和情报机构将罪犯绳之以法。 据报道，内政部表示，这些权力受到严格保障措施约束，政府"从不接触公司的通信系统或数据"。 TCN依据英国《调查权力法》发出。该法禁止任何接收方承认令状的存在或讨论其内容。此类通知可强制企业给英国安全部门提交客户数据，即便这些信息受到高强度加密保护。 英国政府与苹果的争议焦点，是iCloud高级数据保护功能的推出。 这一可选功能对用户iCloud账户内的绝大部分数据加密，包括短信和设备备份。 在收到政府的法律要求后，苹果于2025年2月对英国客户下架了该功能。英国政府则主张，其需要获取用户数据以开展国家安全和刑事调查。 苹果一直为其在产品中使用加密技术辩护。 公司在2023年向英国议会表示，加密"对于保护普通公民免受非法监控、身份盗用、欺诈和数据泄露至关重要"，对可能成为恶意行为者目标的记者、人权活动人士和外交官而言，更是"极其宝贵的保护"。 第二次令状与七月新诉讼 这场拉锯战其实已经打到了第二回合。 据《金融时报》披露，英国政府最早发出第一份秘密令状时，由于要求苹果打开的是针对全球用户的加密“后门”，直接惹恼了保护本国公民与企业数据的华盛顿方面。 据报道，在美方的外交施压下，英国内政部一度被迫退让、放弃了首次尝试。但一年后，英国政府卷土重来，向苹果发出了第二份“技术能力通知”（TCN），苹果随即在7月发起了新一轮法律反击。 与此同时，“隐私国际”（Privacy International）和“自由”（Liberty）两家数字权利倡导组织，也针对政府的保密禁令提起了诉讼。隐私国际法律主管卡罗琳·威尔逊·帕洛称，此次裁决是信息透明与有效监督的“重大胜利”。 她指出，调查权力法庭正确地驳回了政府的借口——苹果是否被迫削弱设备安全性事关重大公共利益，政府不能以未经证实的安全风险为由逃避审查，更不该把“既不确认也不否认”的保密政策当成挡箭牌。 自由组织负责人阿基科·哈特也表示，公众有权知道政府何时损害了他们的隐私与安全，法庭的裁决将让这些秘密监控权力受到更多监督。 尽管英国内政部嘴硬坚称案件的实质问题未受影响，但苹果的诉讼仍在推进。未来几个月，双方真正的硬仗——政府究竟能在多大程度上迫使科技公司为产品留出“访问后门”将在公开法庭上正式打响。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.summary: Anthropic的大规模IPO看上去是对AI交易的信心投票，但彭博经济学家给出了相反的解读。 11月19日，据彭博经济学经济学家Anna Wong的分析，自9月以来，也就是Anthropic招股书所载财务数据的截止期（9月30日），其每百万token的实际价格已大幅下滑。 同期token使用量激增，但市场份额并未随之上升，甚至小幅走低。公司在让渡了相当一部分价格溢价之后，并未换来更强的竞争地位。 简单来说，技 术领先和旺盛的AI需求，并没有转化为持久的定价能力。对投资者而言，这意味着AI交易赖以支撑的估值逻辑，正面临一次来自基本面的检验。 IPO本身会把前沿AI的经济学搬进公开市场。 从此定价、利润率和资本回报将按季度接受审视。回过头看，这场IPO可能不像是AI行情新一轮上涨的起点，而更像是最后一波燃料。 作为前沿模型领域的头部企业、AI热潮的标志性公司，Anthropic暴露出的正是这轮交易核心处的软肋： 前沿智能的定价权正在被削弱。 定价权：护城河究竟由什么构成 持久的护城河，最终要落到攫取经济租金的能力上。Anna Wong的核心论点正建立在这一标准之上： 一家公司能否长期维持高于竞争水平的价格，决定了它的估值是否站得住。 以这一尺度衡量，Anthropic目前呈现的图景并不理想。在招股书财务数据截止前的这段时间里，其有效token价格陡降，价格溢价被大幅让渡，而竞争位置并未因此改善。 技术上的领先优势，没有在价格端兑现为议价能力。 Wong用两张图表概括了整篇论证： 其一 ，每百万token的实际价格近期明显下行； 其二 ，token使用份额并未抬升，反而略有下滑。 价格与份额的这一背离，揭示的是Anthropic所处的市场结构—— 它更像是一个不具备持久定价权的寡头 。增长必须依靠降价来驱动用量，而非依靠产品差异化或客户黏性来支撑价格。Wong写道： 这是一门艰难的生意。 需要说明的是，Anthropic此次巨额融资仍可能在短期内为AI交易再添一把火。资金面的支撑，往往能在情绪层面延续行情。 若定价能力不及估值隐含水平，重估或加速 但IPO的另一面是透明度。 上市之后，定价、利润率和资本回报将逐季披露并被逐季检视，此前只存在于私募市场的定价能力问题，会被摆到公开市场的聚光灯下。 估值所隐含的假设，也将第一次接受连续性数据的对账。 Wong提示的核心风险在于： 如果Anthropic未来的业绩显示，这家公司的定价能力弱于其估值所暗示的水平，那么随之而来的重估，有可能加速AI板块整体估值的回吐。 从更广泛的市场角度看，她近期还指出，根据美联储常用的利率分析模型（Kim and Wright 模型）测算， 目前市场要求的风险补偿（利差）已经明显扩大。 与此同时，在融资条件趋紧的背景下，上一财报季中上市公司提及的 900 多项供应链瓶颈问题仍有大量尚未缓解。这些高频信号共同构成了她对市场与信用风险的持续追踪。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 特朗普9月高位买入英伟达站岗，SpaceX也加仓了

articles.title: Anthropic IPO火爆：超半数机构分文未获，配售向美国投资者高度倾斜
articles.summary: Anthropic的首次公开募股创下历史新高，但极度火爆的需求也意味着绝大多数竞购机构最终空手而归。 据彭博援引知情人士透露， 此次IPO的股份分配向美国本土投资者高度倾斜，超过半数参与认购的机构投资者未获得任何配售。来自美国境外的大量订单几乎被全部忽略，欧洲投资者尤为如此。约1200家机构投资者参与了此次认购。 Anthropic本次IPO连同七位联合创始人合计募资1073亿美元，从SpaceX手中夺得史上最大规模首次公开发行的桂冠。公司的完全摊薄市值定格于1.5万亿美元。 作为美股首家以开发顶尖AI模型为核心业务的公司，Anthropic此次上市具有重要的市场标志性意义。 配售严重向美国本土集中 知情人士称，此次IPO的股份分配呈现出明显的地域偏向，境外订单——尤其是欧洲投资者的订单——获配比例极低乃至为零。 La Financiere de l'Echiquier科技基金经理Christophe Pouchoy表示："在欧洲，参与美国IPO本就很难获得配售，在这种市场热度极高的交易中更是如此。"他指出，"主承销商面对巨大需求不得不做出取舍，绝大多数欧洲投资者最终分文未得。" 相比之下， SpaceX IPO时约有三分之一的认购方未获配售，据彭博当时报道，其竞争激烈程度已属罕见。而Anthropic此次超过半数机构空手而归，争抢烈度更胜一筹。 机构大赢家：头部VC持仓市值合计逾1,500亿美元 Anthropic最大的风险投资方正迎来丰厚回报。 据知情人士透露，Lightspeed Venture Partners与Iconiq均持有Anthropic接近2%的股权，按IPO定价计算，各方持仓市值均超过250亿美元。Lightspeed在该公司累计投入约34亿美元，Iconiq则投入逾60亿美元，两家机构均有望实现数十亿美元的账面收益。 知名度相对较低的基金同样收获颇丰。演员Ashton Kutcher与音乐经纪人Guy Oseary联合创立的Sound Ventures于2023年入股，累计持有约0.5%股权。由前Cruise工程师Sol Bier创立的Factorial Funds，在累计投入5.65亿美元后，账面回报约达19倍。 Menlo Ventures合伙人Matt Murphy及Lightspeed合伙人Ravi Mhatre等早期投资者已专程赴纽约出席纳斯达克的开市钟仪式，并计划在纽约多场私人晚宴上与各方共庆。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 史上最大IPO落地！Anthropic首秀开盘涨34%、市值突破2万亿
articles.summary: AI独角兽又一次创造历史。Anthropic刷新了SpaceX五个月前才创下的上市募资纪录，正式登陆美股，开盘大涨幅度超过此前暗盘预计的最高涨幅，一度将公司市值推升至2万亿美元以上，不过盘中回吐涨幅。 美东时间11月19日周四，Anthropic以ANT为股票代码正式在纳斯达克挂牌交易，开盘报111.50美元，较IPO发行价83美元涨约34.3%，盘中最高触及115.10美元，涨幅扩大到约38.7%，此后一度下探至95.14美元，涨幅收窄至不足15%，后有所回升，曾重上100美元、涨幅扩大到20%以上。 此次Anthropic IPO公开募资约813亿美元，刷新全球IPO募资规模纪录。投资者对Anthropic的追捧，也为AI行业提供了一个重要的资本市场风向标。 发行价对应估值1.5万亿美元，开盘市值超过SpaceX美股首秀 Anthropic此次IPO发行价为每股83美元，明显高于此前70至78美元的指导区间上限，较区间上限高出约6.4%，较74美元的区间中点高出约12.2%，反映出机构投资者需求强劲。 公司此次公开发行约9.8亿股，募资约813亿美元，超过SpaceX此前约750亿美元的IPO募资纪录，成为有史以来规模最大的公开募股。 按照83美元发行价计算，Anthropic完全稀释口径估值约为1.5万亿美元。首笔交易达到111.50美元后，公司对应市值一度突破2万亿美元，较发行价对应的估值增加约5000亿美元。 这一估值不仅超过SpaceX此前上市首秀时约1.77万亿美元的估值，也一度超过Meta、特斯拉和沃尔玛等美国大型上市公司。按照开盘价计算，全球市值超过Anthropic的上市公司仅有苹果、亚马逊、谷歌母公司Alphabet、英伟达和微软等少数巨头。 不过，股价并未维持开盘后的强势。盘中Anthropic股价最高触及115.10美元，随后一度回落至95.14美元，之后又重新回到100美元上方。首日交易仍在进行，市场对这家AI公司的估值博弈尚未结束。 上市前的暗盘交易已经释放出强烈看涨信号。德国券商Lang & Schwarz此前给出的报价一度达到105美元，较发行价溢价26%；加密货币平台Hyperliquid上与Anthropic挂钩的永续期货也曾大幅高于发行价。不过，正式上市后的实际交易显示，投资者对其估值仍存在分歧。 CEO敲钟承诺不屈服于商业和政治压力，强调AI安全及医学突破 在纳斯达克上市仪式上，Anthropic CEO达里奥·阿莫代伊（Dario Amodei）、公司总裁兼联合创始人丹妮拉·阿莫代伊（Daniela Amodei）及其他联合创始人和高管共同敲响开市钟。 Anthropic团队敲钟仪式截图来自纳斯达克 阿莫代伊在讲话中再次强调AI安全是公司的核心使命，并作出明确承诺：Anthropic将根据安全情况决定AI模型的训练和部署节奏，不会为了商业利益或政治压力而牺牲安全标准。 他表示： “我们将控制AI系统的训练和部署节奏，只要有必要，就会持续投入时间，直到我们有信心确认这些系统是安全的，并且能够始终处于人类控制之下。我们不会屈服于商业压力，也不会屈服于政治压力。” 他还强调，此次上市让Anthropic处于更强大的财务地位，但这只会进一步坚定公司坚持正确发展道路的决心。如果能够证明企业既可以坚持安全原则，又能够取得商业上的巨大成功，其他AI公司也会受到激励。他将这种良性竞争称为“向上的竞赛”（Race to the Top）。 除了安全问题，阿莫代伊还描绘了AI在医学研究领域的潜力。他表示，Claude已经帮助蛋白质折叠、药物设计、癌症遗传学和临床试验管理等领域的研究人员大幅缩短研究时间。 他认为，足够强大的AI如果能够与人类协作，有可能将一个世纪的科学和医学进步压缩到十年。不过，他也提醒，目前取得的仍是早期成果，实验和临床试验依然需要时间。 丹妮拉·阿莫代伊则强调，Anthropic从创立之初就将AI安全置于重要位置，公司希望证明，负责任地开发AI与取得商业成功并不矛盾。 年化收入达到810亿美元，企业客户数量快速增长 Anthropic快速扩张的收入和企业客户规模，是此次IPO获得高估值的重要支撑。 监管文件显示，截至2026年10月31日，公司年化运营收入达到810亿美元，较9月底增加约100亿美元。 截至2026年9月底，Anthropic拥有超过11900家过去12个月贡献收入至少10万美元的企业客户，而2025年底这一数字还仅为1500家左右。 公司第三季度营收达到169.56亿美元，较第二季度增长47%。不过，经营层面仍面临压力：第三季度经营亏损约5.67亿美元，而第二季度曾实现经营利润约9.74亿美元。 与此同时，Anthropic在2026年上半年投入近90亿美元用于算力和基础设施，第三季度又产生约50亿美元相关成本。 公司还承诺未来向基础设施合作伙伴支付接近9000亿美元的算力及基础设施费用，其中仅截至2027年9月底的一年内，到期支出就约达710亿美元。 这意味着，Anthropic虽然已经凭借Claude及Claude Code等产品实现收入高速增长，但要支撑未来模型研发和商业化扩张，仍需要持续投入巨额资金。 创纪录IPO检验AI投资热情，后续盈利能力仍是关键 Anthropic的成功上市为AI行业带来了重要的信心信号，但股价开盘后的波动也提醒投资者，创纪录的IPO并不意味着市场对AI公司的高估值已经没有分歧。 Yorkville Ives & Co.合伙人兼董事总经理Dan Ives将此次IPO形容为“A+级的成功”，认为这体现了市场对科技股交易的信心。不过，市场对半导体行业和中国相关问题的担忧仍然存在。 Capital Economics市场经济学家Joe Maher则提醒投资者，不应过度解读新股上市初期的价格跳涨。他认为，Anthropic未来几个月的股价表现，将成为衡量投资者对AI热情的重要试金石。 他指出，Anthropic及其他AI实验室是最终消费者和企业需求进入底层AI供应链的重要渠道，这些公司的算力和数据中心支出，将直接影响大型云计算企业和半导体公司的前景。
